doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: The Duke's Men radio show and the cancelled March 19 concert
summary: Baron describes his Duke's Men gig with Bill Crow and Bernard Purdie, the radio show, the revived management interest, and calling players to cancel.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yes. Also as a band leader, I wonder what it was like for you to have to call your band mates and say —

Well the last gig, this great gig I had for The Duke’s Men, I think I told you about it where I had Bill Crow, the 90 some odd year old bass player, and Bernard Purdie, the great drummer. By the way Purdie swings his butt off. You know I remember meeting him in Richmond, Virginia at a jazz party, oh gosh, probably 30 years ago maybe. And you know these big parties with a whole group of musicians and they put you together. And my first band I played with he was playing drums and I was like oh my God. I told him, we were on radio station BGO right in the beginning of March, before this gig we were to do. And I said, “Pretty, I had to call someone. I think I called my mother.” But anyway so we did it. As a matter of fact I’ll get you a copy of it once I coalesce, once I can make some CDs. We did this radio show on the NPR radio station BGO down here. And it was March 9th. And our gig was on the 19th. And the talk of the pandemic just started talking, just started happening. And the band was great. And I hadn’t led the band in a while and I went back to this management company that gave us great gigs in the late 80s and 90s. And it kind of fizzled out after a while but it was great people. And I knew that a few of them had passed away and a whole new coterie of people were operating it. And at first they weren’t interested but I sent them the information and they said, “Sure, send it.” Then all of a sudden they kind of got excited. So here I was about to do a big concert at this arts center down in Tribeca on the 19th of March and they were going to © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

send one of their agents over. All this was about to happen, and I was like this feels like a resurrection. It feels right. It feels like something to put my time in. And I have this friend of mine named Monk Rowe who got me a gig on October 30, which still are like this. Because I just talked to Purdie last night and I told him about it. Because I wanted to wait just a little more. But good news is better to give than bad news. So so far it’s good news man, and we greatly appreciate that.

But anyway it’s hard when I have to call people up. They know it. They say yeah we pretty much figured this out. But it’s still, it’s, I have to do it person by person and I try to stay away from the email magic you know. I like to call.
